The merge-of-progressions periodicity argument is a reasonable sketch — actually this part is the standard argument: if the tail consists of numbers in a union of residue classes mod $L$ (multiples of $m_H$ with $m_H \mid L$), then the sequence of elements of this union in increasing order is periodic with period $T$ = number of residues and value shift $L$. But there's a subtlety: it needs to be shown that the tail of the sequence actually equals ALL sufficiently large elements of the union (i.e., the greedy doesn't skip or that every element of the union beyond some point appears). Actually, hmm: the greedy picks $a_{n+1}$ = smallest multiple of some $m_H$ greater than $a_n$. Since $a_{N+1}$ is a union element, the sequence from then on enumerates consecutive union elements. Fine.

Actually many solutions establish eventual periodicity and then need the full statement.
